capex_override.ack_reason: The out-of-band flag is mechanical only: the band is computed against the last FILED capex value and RNR has never filed one (last_filed_value is null), so every value flags out-of-band, including the filing-proven $0. The figure is established by the filer's own cash-flow statements (see source), and no filed capex value exists in any period to anchor an estimate to.
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 (and every other year) because the filer does not report a capex line at all; the filer's own cash-flow statements fully account for investing activities in all three years, so capex is $0 as a filing fact, not an estimate (same presentation as the EG/CMPS precedents). Any premises/equipment spend is aggregated inside the filed investing lines and is immaterial at insurer scale — even a hypothetical $50M would move OE by ~$1.08/share (~1.4% of the $77.78 base). The engine's history already carried capex as assumed-zero, so the override changes no OE figure; it converts a silent zero-fill into a sourced, registered decision.
capex_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-11, accession 0000913144-26-000012), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (p. F-8): the investing-activities section lists only fixed-maturity / short-term / equity / other investment flows, derivatives settlements, investments in other ventures and the Validus purchase — there is no purchases-of-property-and-equipment (or any capex) line for FY2025, FY2024 or FY2023, and the Consolidated Balance Sheets (p. F-5) carry no property-and-equipment line. The statement fully reconciles without one: FY2025 operating $3,693,107 thousand + investing $(2,215,809) thousand + financing $(1,410,503) thousand + FX $(12,218) thousand = the reported net increase in cash of $54,577 thousand exactly; FY2024: $4,164,822 - $3,060,856 - $1,287,515 - $17,365 = reported $(200,914) thousand exactly; FY2023: $1,911,634 - $3,822,636 + $2,588,639 + $5,542 = reported $683,179 thousand exactly. EDGAR companyfacts for CIK 913144 contains no capex fact under any candidate tag in any year.

moat_against: Reinsurance capacity is close to a commodity — no network effects, low switching costs, price set by the cycle; property-cat pricing fell high-teens at mid-2026 renewals
Catastrophe earnings volatility: net losses in 2021 and 2022 (2022 attributable net loss $1,061M) — a single severe cat year can erase several benign years of OE
Casualty & specialty is the weak leg: 103.3% combined ratio and an underwriting loss in Q2 2026, adverse prior-year development, social-inflation exposure
Reserve risk is the balance sheet: $22,302M of claim reserves at Dec 31, 2025 are estimates, and prior-year development swings earnings both ways

Third-party capital is rented, not owned — partner capital takes its share of the best underwriting economics ($935M of FY2025 net income attributable to redeemable noncontrolling interests) and can be returned at cycle turns
moat_for: Leading global property-catastrophe reinsurance franchise — 72.8% combined ratio in Q2 2026, book value per share +24.8% YoY to $264.77
Capital Partners third-party capital platform: >$9B of partner/ILS capital at Dec 31, 2025 and $328.9M of FY2025 fee income — capacity and fees peers cannot easily replicate
Validus Re acquisition (closed Nov 1, 2023) added treaty scale and diversification into casualty & specialty
Disciplined cycle management — gross premiums written down 12.5% YoY in Q2 2026 into softening prices, more retrocession bought instead of chasing share
Aggressive, accretive buybacks: ~11.5M shares (~22% of the starting count) repurchased for ~$3B over the two years to Q2 2026
moat_justification: A top-tier global property-catastrophe reinsurance franchise plus the Capital Partners third-party capital platform (third-party capital of just over $9B at December 31, 2025, ~$8.5B at mid-2026; fee income $328.9M in FY2025 and $83.0M in Q2 2026) are real differentiators — RenRe matches efficient capital to risk and earns a fee stream peers without a comparable ILS/joint-venture platform do not. But reinsurance capacity itself is close to a commodity: no network effects, low switching costs, price set by the cycle, and pricing is now softening (U.S. property-catastrophe rates down high-teens at the mid-2026 renewals). Returns confirm a narrow moat: attributable net income on year-end equity was strongly positive in the hard-market years 2023-2025 ($2,561M / $9,455M, $1,870M / $10,574M, $2,682M / $11,609M) but the company lost $1,061M in 2022 and $40M in 2021 — through a full cycle, returns swing around the cost of capital rather than staying well above it. roic_proxy and gross margin are not computable for this filer (fundamentals.json carries no operating-income/COGS series for an insurer); ROE on filing net income and equity is the substitute evidence.
name: RenaissanceRe Holdings Ltd.
one_liner: Global property-catastrophe reinsurer with a real Capital Partners fee franchise, moat 5/10 — engine prints Tier S (weighted IRR 27.31%, IV@15% $720.19 vs $351.06) on an OCF base that capitalizes float and noncontrolling-interest cash flow, so the final tier is softened to A at low confidence; on engine numbers it clears 15% at ~$720, ~$553 (bear IV) with a margin of safety.

base_override.source: Operating income (loss) available to RenaissanceRe common shareholders, twelve months ended December 31, from the company's Q4 earnings releases (Form 8-K exhibit 99.1): FY2021 $81,599 thousand (release filed 2022-02, accession 0000913144-22-000010); FY2022 $322,791 thousand and FY2023 $1,824,910 thousand (FY2023 release, accession 0000913144-24-000005); FY2024 $2,234,426 thousand and FY2025 $1,859,691 thousand (FY2025 release, accession 0000913144-26-000003). Denominator: FY2025 diluted shares 46,483,000 (financials_history.csv shares_diluted, latest row; the same release's 'Average shares outstanding - diluted').
base_override.reason: Insurer payable-earnings base (Andrew, 2026-10-19; WORKER_SPEC step 4): consolidated OCF at a reinsurer capitalizes the reserve build ($998,854,000 in FY2025) and the cash earned by consolidated Capital Partners vehicles ($935,409,000 of FY2025 net income attributable to redeemable noncontrolling interests), so the engine's $77.78/sh median base is not what common shareholders earn. Construction: ($81,599 + $322,791 + $1,824,910 + $2,234,426 + $1,859,691) thousand = $6,323,417 thousand; / 5 = $1,264,683.4 thousand; / 46,483 thousand diluted shares = $27.2074/share. Five-year average rather than 3-year median because FY2023-25 are three benign-cat hard-market years and FY2021-22 are the cycle's loss years (combined ratios 102.1% / 97.7%). Replaces the 2026-10-15 one-notch tier softening, which is not applied on top of this base.
